c.tagline: Desert futurism reaching for the sky.

avoid.reason: Watch for fake-goods touts in Deira's souks and occasional taxi/rental overcharging, and stay mindful of strict laws on public behavior and photography.

hood_desc: The glittering center anchored by the Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall with luxury hotels and the dancing fountains, ideal for upscale travelers, shoppers, and first-time sightseers.
A glamorous waterfront district of high-rise towers, yachts, beach clubs, and a lively promenade, suiting nightlife lovers, beachgoers, and young travelers.
An upscale coastal area of villas, pristine public beaches, and the Burj Al Arab, perfect for beach lovers and luxury travelers wanting a relaxed seaside vibe.
The atmospheric old-Dubai district of traditional souks, spice and gold markets, and the creek, great for budget travelers and those seeking the city's heritage and bargains.
A modern high-rise business and hotel district beside the canal, home to sleek towers and dining, appealing to business travelers and those wanting a central contemporary base.
lodging: Radisson Blu Hotel, Dubai Deira Creek

water.note: Desalinated tap water is treated and safe to drink, though many prefer bottled for taste.

transit.pay: You need a nol card for the metro, tram and buses — bank cards can't be tapped at the gates yet (planned for 2027). Buy a silver nol card for AED 25 (~US$7, includes AED 19 credit) at metro station machines and counters, including at the airport, and top up via machines or the nol Pay app.
transit.hours: The Metro runs about 5am to midnight (until 1am Friday nights) and from 8am on Sundays; the tram runs 6am to 1am.

landmarks: Burj Khalifa
The tallest building in the world at over 828 meters, its observation decks offer unmatched views over the city and desert.
Burj Al Arab
Shaped like a billowing sail on its own artificial island, this ultra-luxury hotel is one of the most recognizable silhouettes in the world.
The Dubai Fountain
Set on the Burj Khalifa Lake, this is the world's largest choreographed fountain system, with jets synced to music and colored lights each evening.
Palm Jumeirah
A man-made archipelago shaped like a palm tree, visible from space, lined with resorts and best photographed from the air or its observation deck.
The Dubai Mall
One of the largest shopping malls on Earth, home to an enormous aquarium, ice rink, and waterfall sculpture alongside hundreds of stores.
Dubai Frame
A giant gold-rimmed picture-frame structure that lets visitors look out over both old and new Dubai from a glass-floored skybridge.
Museum of the Future
A striking torus-shaped, calligraphy-clad building that has become an instant architectural icon of futuristic Dubai.
Atlantis, The Palm
This pink-domed resort at the tip of Palm Jumeirah is famous for its waterpark, aquarium, and grand Arabian-style architecture.
Dubai Marina
A dense skyline of waterfront skyscrapers along an artificial canal, popular for its promenade, yacht-lined marina, and nighttime skyline views.
Jumeirah Mosque
One of the few mosques in the UAE open to non-Muslim visitors, its intricate Fatimid-style architecture makes it a favorite photography subject.

train.note: Dubai has no passenger trains yet. Etihad Rail's first UAE passenger service (Abu Dhabi-Fujairah) started 30 June 2026, and Dubai's own station is due to open on 30 September 2026 - until then travel by intercity bus. The Dubai Metro is urban only.

bus.note: The Dubai-Muscat coaches take about 6-7 hours via the Hatta border; buy tickets at the Abu Hail/Deira offices or online and bring your passport - check Oman visa rules first. Frequent domestic E-buses to Abu Dhabi and other emirates leave from Al Ghubaiba and Union stations.

ferry.note: No scheduled international ferries could be confirmed from Dubai for 2026. Passenger boats between the UAE and Iran (Valfajr line, via Sharjah/Dubai to Bandar Lengeh) have run on and off in recent years but are unreliable - check locally before planning around them. RTA's Dubai Ferry is a local commuter/sightseeing service.

half.name: Abu Dhabi
half.blurb: The capital draws crowds for the vast Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque and waterfront corniche.

half.name: Hatta
half.blurb: This mountain enclave offers a turquoise dam, kayaking and rugged hiking trails.

half.name: Al Ain
half.blurb: The garden city is known for oases, a historic fort and the Jebel Hafeet mountain drive.

half.name: Sharjah
half.blurb: The cultural capital is famed for its museums, heritage souks and Islamic art.

half.name: Ras Al Khaimah
half.blurb: Adventurers head here for Jebel Jais peaks, the world's longest zipline and quiet beaches.

half.name: Fujairah
half.blurb: The east coast lures divers and beachgoers to Snoopy Island and Al Aqah's clear waters.
